tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

165	### 4.2 LinearRegression 的 coef_ / intercept_ 与正规方程
166	
167	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
168	
169	梯度下降是**迭代逼近**，但线性回归的 MSE 是凸函数，其实存在**一步到位的解析解**（closed-form solution），即著名的**最小二乘法 / 正规方程（normal equations）**：在 X 前面拼一列 1（吸收截距），则
170	
171	\[
172	\hat w = (X_b^T X_b)^{-1} X_b^T y
173	\]
174	
175	sklearn 的 `LinearRegression` 内部基于最小二乘求解（实际用更数值稳定的 SVD 实现，不需要调学习率、也不需要标准化）。训练后它把学到的参数放在两个属性里：
176	
177	- `coef_`：斜率数组（每个特征一个系数）；
178	- `intercept_`：截距标量。
179	
180	注意命名差异：手写类叫 `w_` / `b_`，sklearn 叫 `coef_` / `intercept_`——后者是 sklearn 线性模型家族（后面 u9-l2 的 Ridge、Lasso 也一样）的统一约定。
181	
182	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
183	
184	```text
185	X（原始尺度，n×1）、y（原始尺度，美元）
186	    ↓
187	slr = LinearRegression(); slr.fit(X, y)     # 解析解，无需 eta、无需标准化
188	    ↓
189	slr.coef_       # 斜率：每增加 1 平方英尺，房价平均增加多少美元
190	slr.intercept_  # 截距：面积为 0 时的“基准价”（只是数学外推，未必有现实意义）
191	    ↓
192	验证：手工实现正规方程 (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy，两边的斜率/截距应完全一致
193	```

257	### 4.3 RANSACRegressor：离群掩码与鲁棒回归
258	
259	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
260	
261	回头看 4.2 的散点图：数据云里混着一些「面积很大却卖得极便宜」的点（数据文档说明这类异常成交确实存在）。MSE 用平方惩罚误差，这些离群点会强烈拉扯回归线。**RANSAC（随机样本共识）**换了一种思路：
262	
263	1. 随机抽一小撮样本拟合一个候选模型；
264	2. 用候选模型检查**全体**样本：残差小于阈值 `residual_threshold` 的算「一致者」（inliers，内点），其余算「离群者」（outliers）；
265	3. 重复 `max_trials` 轮，保留**内点最多**的那个候选；
266	4. 最后**只用内点**重新拟合，得到最终模型。
267	
268	直觉：真实趋势由「大多数正常点」决定，离群点因为无法和大多数点同时达成一致，会自然被淘汰。RANSAC 不改变基模型（仍是 `LinearRegression`），只改变「用哪些样本去拟合」，因此属于**鲁棒回归**的元算法。拟合结束后，每个样本是否为内点记录在 `inlier_mask_`（布尔数组，长度等于样本数）——这就是本模块标题里的「离群掩码」，用它做 `np.logical_not` 即得离群点掩码。
269	
270	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
271	
272	```text
273	RANSACRegressor(LinearRegression(),
274	                max_trials=100,        # 最多尝试 100 个候选模型
275	                min_samples=0.95,      # 每轮随机抽取 95% 的样本拟合候选
276	                loss='absolute_error', # 用绝对误差（而非平方）衡量残差
277	                residual_threshold=None,  # None → 用 y 的 MAD 自动定阈值
278	                random_state=123)
279	    ↓ fit(X, y)
280	每轮：随机抽 min_samples 比例的样本 → 拟合候选直线 → 数内点
281	    ↓
282	保留内点最多者 → 用其内点集合重拟合 → estimator_（最终的 LinearRegression）
283	    ↓
284	ransac.inlier_mask_      # 布尔掩码：True=内点
285	outlier_mask = np.logical_not(inlier_mask)
286	    ↓
287	ransac.estimator_.coef_ / .intercept_   # 只属于内点的回归系数
288	```
289	
290	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
291	
292	**构造与拟合**（[ch09/ch09.py:L352-L360](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch09/ch09.py#L352-L360)）：五个参数逐一看——`max_trials=100` 是默认值；`min_samples=0.95` 以比例形式传入，表示每轮随机抽约 95% 的样本参与拟合候选模型（取大头是为了让候选更稳，代价是「最小抽样」的随机性减弱）；`loss='absolute_error'` 用绝对误差计残差，天然比平方误差对大偏差更不敏感；`residual_threshold=None` 交给 sklearn 自动估计——默认用目标值 y 的 **MAD（median absolute deviation，中位数绝对偏差）**，即 \( \mathrm{median}(|y_i - \mathrm{median}(y)|) \)，比标准差更抗离群点污染。

339	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
340	
341	**练习 1**：RANSAC 改变了基模型 `LinearRegression` 本身吗？最终用于预测的模型存在哪个属性里？
342	
343	答案：没有改变。RANSAC 是包裹在基模型外的元算法，负责挑选「用哪些样本」拟合；最终只用内点重拟合出的 `LinearRegression` 存在 `ransac.estimator_` 中，`ransac.predict` 内部就是调用它。
344	
345	**练习 2**：为什么 `loss` 选 `'absolute_error'` 而不是平方误差？`residual_threshold=None` 时 sklearn 用什么统计量定阈值、它为何抗离群？
346	
347	答案：绝对误差对大残差不平方放大，让「数内点」这一步不被个别巨离样本牵制；阈值为 None 时用 y 的中位数绝对偏差 MAD = median(|y − median(y)|)，中位数本身不受极端值影响，因此用它估计「正常波动范围」比标准差稳健。
348	
349	**练习 3**：如果 `residual_threshold` 设得极大（比如 \(10^9\)），RANSAC 会退化成什么？
350	
351	答案：所有样本残差都小于阈值、全部算内点，内点数恒为最大值，第一次随机子集拟合的模型就会被保留——结果近似于（但随机子集上的）普通最小二乘，RANSAC 的鲁棒性完全失效。
352	
353	### 4.4 残差图与 MSE / R² 诊断
354	
355	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
356	
357	模型拟合完了，怎么知道它好不好？回归诊断有两层：
358	
359	**一层是「看图」——残差图（residual plot）**。横轴为预测值 \(\hat y\)、纵轴为残差 \( y - \hat y \)，并画一条 0 参考线。理想形态：点随机均匀散布在 0 线两侧、无明显形状。三种典型病灶：
360	
361	- 残差随 \(\hat y\) 增大而发散（**漏斗形**）→ 异方差，误差方差不等；
362	- 残差呈弯曲的带状 → 存在非线性关系，直线不够用（u9-l2 会用多项式、树模型解决）；
363	- 个别点残差巨大 → 离群点，正是 4.3 RANSAC 处理的对象。
364	
365	**另一层是「算数」——三个指标**：
366	
367	\[ \mathrm{MSE} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (y^{(i)} - \hat y^{(i)})^2, \qquad
368	\mathrm{MAE} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |y^{(i)} - \hat y^{(i)}| \]
369	
370	\[ R^2 = 1 - \frac{SS_{res}}{SS_{tot}} = 1 - \frac{\sum_i (y^{(i)} - \hat y^{(i)})^2}{\sum_i (y^{(i)} - \bar y)^2} \]
371	
372	MSE / MAE 的量纲是美元的平方 / 美元，**只能在同一数据集上横向比较模型**；R² 则回答「比起『无脑预测均值』这个基准，模型把不可解释的方差减少了多少」：1 为完美，0 等于均值基准，越接近 1 越好。注意 MSE 对大误差平方放大（受离群点影响大），MAE 更贴近「平均差多少钱」的直觉。这一节还把模型从 1 个特征扩到全部 5 个特征，并首次引入**训练集 / 测试集划分**——防止「训练集上拟合得好」误导我们（思想承接 u6-l1 的评估纪律）。
373	
374	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
375	
376	```text
377	X = 全部 5 个特征（含编码后的 Central Air）；y = SalePrice
378	    ↓
379	train_test_split(test_size=0.3, random_state=123)   # 注意：未 stratify（回归无类别可分层）
380	    ↓
381	LinearRegression().fit(X_train) → y_train_pred / y_test_pred
382	    ↓
383	残差图：左子图测试集、右子图训练集，散点 (ŷ, ŷ − y)，加 y=0 参考线
384	    ↓
385	mean_squared_error / mean_absolute_error / r2_score 分别在 train、test 上计算
386	```
387	
388	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
389

391	
392	**拟合与预测**（[ch09/ch09.py:L454-L458](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch09/ch09.py#L454-L458)）：对训练集 `fit`，然后**分别**对训练集与测试集 `predict`——评估的要义是同一模型在两套数据上的对照。

427	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
428

431	答案：训练 / 测试差距大是典型**高方差（过拟合）**。可尝试：减少特征或用 u9-l2 的正则化（Ridge/Lasso）收缩系数、收集更多数据、换更简单的模型。残差图上训练集残差应明显更小。
432	
433	**练习 2**：为什么 R² 的基准（\(SS_{tot}\) 用均值预测）让它「天然抗盲目乐观」？R² 可能为负吗？

# u9-l1 线性回归与 RANSAC

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 理解**回归（regression）**与分类的区别：预测的目标变量从「离散类别」变成了「连续数值」。
2. 逐行读懂手写的 `LinearRegressionGD` 类，看明白「回归版梯度下降」的更新式，并意识到它与第 2 章的 `AdalineGD` 在数学上完全同构。
3. 会用 scikit-learn 的 `LinearRegression`，读懂它给出的斜率 `coef_` 与截距 `intercept_`，并用书中附带的「正规方程」手工算一遍验证两者一致。
4. 理解离群点如何把普通最小二乘的回归线「拉歪」，以及 `RANSACRegressor` 如何用 `inlier_mask_`（内点掩码）把离群点排除在拟合之外。
5. 学会用**残差图**和 MSE / MAE / R² 三类指标诊断一个回归模型的好坏。

本讲源码集中在 `ch09/ch09.py` 的 L212–L514（手写梯度下降 → sklearn 线性回归 → RANSAC → 评估），后面的正则化回归与树回归留给 u9-l2。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲默认你已读过前面几讲的概念，先快速回顾，再补充回归特有的新概念。

**已学过的（简要回顾）：**

- **梯度下降**（u2-l2）：整批梯度下降每轮用全部样本算一次梯度，更新式为 \( w \leftarrow w + \eta \cdot \frac{2}{n} X^T(y - \hat{y}) \)；学习率 \(\eta\) 是最敏感的超参数，特征未缩放时极易发散。
- **标准化**（u2-l3、u6-l1）：`StandardScaler` 把每列特征变成均值 0、方差 1；参数只能在训练集上 `fit`，新数据只做 `transform`。
- **估计器范式**（u3-l1）：sklearn 的模型统一走 `fit` / `predict` 接口，`LinearRegression` 与之前的分类器用法完全一致。

**本讲新增的概念：**

1. **回归 vs 分类**。前面预测的是鸢尾花品种、肿瘤良恶性这类**离散标签**；本讲预测的是房价这类**连续数值**。模型的输出不再是类别编号，而是一个实数，因此评估方式也从「准确率」换成 MSE、R² 等数值误差指标。

2. **简单线性回归模型**。用一条直线（多元时是超平面）拟合数据：

   \[ y = w_1 x_1 + w_2 x_2 + \dots + w_m x_m + b + \epsilon \]

   其中 \( w \) 是权重（回归里叫**斜率 / 系数**），\( b \) 是偏置（**截距**），\( \epsilon \) 是无法解释的噪声。训练目标是最小化**均方误差（MSE，即平方误差和 SSE 的平均）**：

   \[ J(w, b) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(y^{(i)} - \hat{y}^{(i)}\right)^2 \]

   只用一个特征（如居住面积）预测房价叫**简单线性回归**，用多个特征叫**多元线性回归**。

3. **残差（residual）**。单个样本的预测误差 \( y^{(i)} - \hat{y}^{(i)} \)。把残差画成图是回归里最重要的诊断工具：好的模型残差应随机散布在 0 附近，若残差呈漏斗形或曲线形，说明模型有问题（详见 4.4）。

4. **离群点（outlier）与鲁棒回归**。MSE 对误差取平方，误差被平方放大——一个偏离 30 万美元的豪宅能把整条回归线拉向自己。RANSAC（RANdom SAmple Consensus，随机样本共识）通过反复随机抽样、只信任「大多数点都同意」的模型，自动识别并剔除离群点（详见 4.3）。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 LinearRegressionGD：回归版梯度下降

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

怎么找到让 MSE 最小的 \( w \) 和 \( b \)？第 2 章我们已经学过一个工具：**梯度下降**——沿着代价函数的负梯度方向一小步一小步往下走。本模块的手写类 `LinearRegressionGD` 就是把这套思路原封不动搬到回归任务上。

一个值得先建立的直觉：这个类与第 2 章的 `AdalineGD` 几乎是**同一个东西**。`AdalineGD` 训练时用恒等激活函数、以 SSE 为代价，这两点正是线性回归的定义；区别只在用途——`AdalineGD` 在 `predict` 里加了个 0.5 阈值把连续输出切成 0/1 类别（分类器），而 `LinearRegressionGD` 的 `predict` 直接返回连续值（回归器）。对照读这两个类，你会对「分类与回归共享同一套线性模型 + 梯度下降骨架」有更深的体会。

另外一个关键点：**必须先标准化**。`SalePrice` 的量级是 \(10^5\) 美元，`Gr Liv Area` 的量级是 \(10^3\) 平方英尺，代价曲面会扁得像峡谷，学习率稍大就发散（和 u2-l2 的实验结论一致）。所以代码对 X 和 y **分别**用 `StandardScaler` 缩放，预测完再用 `inverse_transform` 把标准化尺度上的预测值换算回美元。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
读入 Ames 数据 → 取 X = Gr Liv Area（n×1）、y = SalePrice（n,）
    ↓
sc_x.fit_transform(X)          # 特征标准化
sc_y.fit_transform(y[:, None]).flatten()   # 目标也标准化（二维进、一维出）
    ↓
LinearRegressionGD(eta=0.1).fit(X_std, y_std)
    每轮 epoch：
      output = X·w + b                    # 全体样本的预测
      errors = y - output                 # 残差向量
      w ← w + η · (2/n) · Xᵀ·errors       # 权重沿负梯度更新
      b ← b + η · 2 · errors.mean()       # 截距更新
      losses_.append( (errors**2).mean() )  # 记录本轮 MSE
    ↓
画 epoch–MSE 曲线；lin_regplot 画散点 + 回归线
    ↓
预测 2500 平方英尺的房价：先 transform 到标准化尺度 → predict → inverse_transform 还原成美元
```

其中梯度更新式来自对 MSE 求偏导（对照 u2-l2 的推导，只是把激活函数换成恒等）：

\[
\frac{\partial J}{\partial w} = -\frac{2}{n}X^T(y - \hat y), \qquad
\frac{\partial J}{\partial b} = -\frac{2}{n}\sum_i (y^{(i)} - \hat y^{(i)})
\]

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**类的全貌**（[ch09/ch09.py:L212-L237](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch09/ch09.py#L212-L237)）：整个 `LinearRegressionGD` 只有三个方法——`fit`（训练）、`net_input`（线性输出 \( Xw+b \)）、`predict`（直接返回 `net_input`，没有任何阈值或激活）。对比 `AdalineGD` 的定义 [ch02/ch02.py:L307-L390](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch02/ch02.py#L307-L390)，你会发现它连 docstring 都更短——因为回归不需要讲激活函数的故事。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`LinearRegressionGD.predict` 与 `AdalineGD.predict` 的返回值有什么本质区别？各自的用途是什么？

答案：`LinearRegressionGD.predict` 直接返回 `net_input` 的连续值（房价），用于回归；`AdalineGD.predict` 在净输入上套阈值函数（大于 0.5 返回 1，否则 0），把连续值离散成类别，用于分类。两者的训练代码几乎相同，差别全在预测端的这一步离散化。

**练习 2**：为什么标准化后训练出的截距 `b_` 几乎等于 0？

答案：标准化后 \(\bar x = 0\)、\(\bar y = 0\)，而最小二乘解必然满足回归线穿过样本中心 \((\bar x, \bar y)\)，即 \( \bar y = w\bar x + b \Rightarrow 0 = 0 + b \)，所以 \( b = 0 \)。

**练习 3**：`fit` 里为什么把权重初始化为很小的随机数（scale=0.01）而不是 0？

答案：对单特征线性回归来说全零初始化其实也能收敛（梯度不为零）；小随机初始化是神经网络时代的通用习惯——对多特征回归，全零初始化的各权重梯度仍然不同（依赖各自特征列），尚可工作，但在多层网络里全零初始化会让所有神经元学到相同的东西。这里沿用该习惯并同时用 `random_state` 固定随机种子保证可复现。

### 4.2 LinearRegression 的 coef_ / intercept_ 与正规方程

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

梯度下降是**迭代逼近**，但线性回归的 MSE 是凸函数，其实存在**一步到位的解析解**（closed-form solution），即著名的**最小二乘法 / 正规方程（normal equations）**：在 X 前面拼一列 1（吸收截距），则

\[
\hat w = (X_b^T X_b)^{-1} X_b^T y
\]

sklearn 的 `LinearRegression` 内部基于最小二乘求解（实际用更数值稳定的 SVD 实现，不需要调学习率、也不需要标准化）。训练后它把学到的参数放在两个属性里：

- `coef_`：斜率数组（每个特征一个系数）；
- `intercept_`：截距标量。

注意命名差异：手写类叫 `w_` / `b_`，sklearn 叫 `coef_` / `intercept_`——后者是 sklearn 线性模型家族（后面 u9-l2 的 Ridge、Lasso 也一样）的统一约定。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
X（原始尺度，n×1）、y（原始尺度，美元）
    ↓
slr = LinearRegression(); slr.fit(X, y)     # 解析解，无需 eta、无需标准化
    ↓
slr.coef_       # 斜率：每增加 1 平方英尺，房价平均增加多少美元
slr.intercept_  # 截距：面积为 0 时的“基准价”（只是数学外推，未必有现实意义）
    ↓
验证：手工实现正规方程 (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy，两边的斜率/截距应完全一致
```

```python

slr.fit(X, y)
y_pred = slr.predict(X)
print(f'Slope: {slr.coef_[0]:.3f}')
print(f'Intercept: {slr.intercept_:.3f}')
```

notebook 真实输出：`Slope: 111.666, Intercept: 13342.979`。斜率可直接解读为「其他条件不变时，居住面积每多 1 平方英尺，房价平均高约 111.7 美元」——**系数可解释性**正是线性回归在房价分析中长盛不衰的原因。注意这里用的是**原始尺度**的 X、y：解析解不需要学习率，标准化与否只影响参数的数值表达，不影响拟合的直线本身（本例单特征时拟合的直线在原始坐标系里完全一致，斜率不同只是坐标系不同）。

```python
w = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
z = np.linalg.inv(np.dot(Xb.T, Xb))
w = np.dot(z, np.dot(Xb.T, y))
```

这段「加一列 1 → 求 \((X_b^T X_b)^{-1}\) → 乘 \(X_b^T y\)」的代码输出 `Slope: 111.666, Intercept: 13342.979`，与 sklearn 完全一致——验证了 `LinearRegression` 就是最小二乘解析解的实现。

### 4.3 RANSACRegressor：离群掩码与鲁棒回归

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

回头看 4.2 的散点图：数据云里混着一些「面积很大却卖得极便宜」的点（数据文档说明这类异常成交确实存在）。MSE 用平方惩罚误差，这些离群点会强烈拉扯回归线。**RANSAC（随机样本共识）**换了一种思路：

1. 随机抽一小撮样本拟合一个候选模型；
2. 用候选模型检查**全体**样本：残差小于阈值 `residual_threshold` 的算「一致者」（inliers，内点），其余算「离群者」（outliers）；
3. 重复 `max_trials` 轮，保留**内点最多**的那个候选；
4. 最后**只用内点**重新拟合，得到最终模型。

直觉：真实趋势由「大多数正常点」决定，离群点因为无法和大多数点同时达成一致，会自然被淘汰。RANSAC 不改变基模型（仍是 `LinearRegression`），只改变「用哪些样本去拟合」，因此属于**鲁棒回归**的元算法。拟合结束后，每个样本是否为内点记录在 `inlier_mask_`（布尔数组，长度等于样本数）——这就是本模块标题里的「离群掩码」，用它做 `np.logical_not` 即得离群点掩码。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
RANSACRegressor(LinearRegression(),
                max_trials=100,        # 最多尝试 100 个候选模型
                min_samples=0.95,      # 每轮随机抽取 95% 的样本拟合候选
                loss='absolute_error', # 用绝对误差（而非平方）衡量残差
                residual_threshold=None,  # None → 用 y 的 MAD 自动定阈值
                random_state=123)
    ↓ fit(X, y)
每轮：随机抽 min_samples 比例的样本 → 拟合候选直线 → 数内点
    ↓
保留内点最多者 → 用其内点集合重拟合 → estimator_（最终的 LinearRegression）
    ↓
ransac.inlier_mask_      # 布尔掩码：True=内点
outlier_mask = np.logical_not(inlier_mask)
    ↓
ransac.estimator_.coef_ / .intercept_   # 只属于内点的回归系数
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**构造与拟合**（[ch09/ch09.py:L352-L360](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch09/ch09.py#L352-L360)）：五个参数逐一看——`max_trials=100` 是默认值；`min_samples=0.95` 以比例形式传入，表示每轮随机抽约 95% 的样本参与拟合候选模型（取大头是为了让候选更稳，代价是「最小抽样」的随机性减弱）；`loss='absolute_error'` 用绝对误差计残差，天然比平方误差对大偏差更不敏感；`residual_threshold=None` 交给 sklearn 自动估计——默认用目标值 y 的 **MAD（median absolute deviation，中位数绝对偏差）**，即 \( \mathrm{median}(|y_i - \mathrm{median}(y)|) \)，比标准差更抗离群点污染。

**掩码的提取**（[ch09/ch09.py:L362-L363](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch09/ch09.py#L362-L363)）：

```python

outlier_mask = np.logical_not(inlier_mask)
```

`inlier_mask_` 是与样本等长的布尔数组；`np.logical_not` 按位取反得到离群掩码。这两个掩码既是可视化工具，也可以导出做进一步的数据审查。

**内点/离群点分色可视化**（[ch09/ch09.py:L365-L380](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch09/ch09.py#L365-L380)）：用 `X[inlier_mask]`、`X[outlier_mask]` 布尔索引把两群点分别画成蓝色圆点与绿色方块（见配图 [figures/09_09.png](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch09/figures/09_09.png)），再叠加 `ransac.predict` 的回归线。**注意一个代码细节**：`line_X = np.arange(3, 10, 1)` 只覆盖 x∈[3, 9]，而 `Gr Liv Area` 的实际范围是 334–5 642 平方英尺，这条黑线在图上几乎缩在原点处不可见——推测是作者从本书前版（对应特征的取值恰在该区间的数据集）沿袭下来的遗留写法，实践中建议改成 `np.arange(X.min(), X.max()+1, 100)` 之类覆盖数据范围的网格（综合实践里我们会修正它）。

```python
    return np.mean(np.abs(data - np.mean(data)))
```

这个小工具算的是 y 相对其**均值**的平均绝对偏差，用来感受「目标值的典型波动量级」，帮助人工选阈值。注意它名字里的 deviation 是均值口径，与 sklearn 内部（`residual_threshold=None` 时）用的**中位数**口径 MAD 是两个不同的统计量，不要混淆。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：RANSAC 改变了基模型 `LinearRegression` 本身吗？最终用于预测的模型存在哪个属性里？

答案：没有改变。RANSAC 是包裹在基模型外的元算法，负责挑选「用哪些样本」拟合；最终只用内点重拟合出的 `LinearRegression` 存在 `ransac.estimator_` 中，`ransac.predict` 内部就是调用它。

**练习 2**：为什么 `loss` 选 `'absolute_error'` 而不是平方误差？`residual_threshold=None` 时 sklearn 用什么统计量定阈值、它为何抗离群？

答案：绝对误差对大残差不平方放大，让「数内点」这一步不被个别巨离样本牵制；阈值为 None 时用 y 的中位数绝对偏差 MAD = median(|y − median(y)|)，中位数本身不受极端值影响，因此用它估计「正常波动范围」比标准差稳健。

**练习 3**：如果 `residual_threshold` 设得极大（比如 \(10^9\)），RANSAC 会退化成什么？

答案：所有样本残差都小于阈值、全部算内点，内点数恒为最大值，第一次随机子集拟合的模型就会被保留——结果近似于（但随机子集上的）普通最小二乘，RANSAC 的鲁棒性完全失效。

### 4.4 残差图与 MSE / R² 诊断

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

模型拟合完了，怎么知道它好不好？回归诊断有两层：

**一层是「看图」——残差图（residual plot）**。横轴为预测值 \(\hat y\)、纵轴为残差 \( y - \hat y \)，并画一条 0 参考线。理想形态：点随机均匀散布在 0 线两侧、无明显形状。三种典型病灶：

- 残差随 \(\hat y\) 增大而发散（**漏斗形**）→ 异方差，误差方差不等；
- 残差呈弯曲的带状 → 存在非线性关系，直线不够用（u9-l2 会用多项式、树模型解决）；
- 个别点残差巨大 → 离群点，正是 4.3 RANSAC 处理的对象。

**另一层是「算数」——三个指标**：

\[ \mathrm{MSE} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (y^{(i)} - \hat y^{(i)})^2, \qquad
\mathrm{MAE} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |y^{(i)} - \hat y^{(i)}| \]

\[ R^2 = 1 - \frac{SS_{res}}{SS_{tot}} = 1 - \frac{\sum_i (y^{(i)} - \hat y^{(i)})^2}{\sum_i (y^{(i)} - \bar y)^2} \]

MSE / MAE 的量纲是美元的平方 / 美元，**只能在同一数据集上横向比较模型**；R² 则回答「比起『无脑预测均值』这个基准，模型把不可解释的方差减少了多少」：1 为完美，0 等于均值基准，越接近 1 越好。注意 MSE 对大误差平方放大（受离群点影响大），MAE 更贴近「平均差多少钱」的直觉。这一节还把模型从 1 个特征扩到全部 5 个特征，并首次引入**训练集 / 测试集划分**——防止「训练集上拟合得好」误导我们（思想承接 u6-l1 的评估纪律）。

```text
    ↓
LinearRegression().fit(X_train) → y_train_pred / y_test_pred
```

**练习 2**：为什么 R² 的基准（\(SS_{tot}\) 用均值预测）让它「天然抗盲目乐观」？R² 可能为负吗？

答案：\(SS_{tot}\) 是「永远预测样本均值」这一最笨模型的残差平方和；R² 度量的是相对它的改进，若模型连均值基准都不如（\(SS_{res} > SS_{tot}\)），R² 为负。在训练集上 R² ≥ 0（最小二乘不会差过均值），但在测试集上完全可能为负——这本身就是过拟合的报警信号。

**练习 3**：本节 `train_test_split` 为什么不像 u6-l1 那样传 `stratify=y`？

答案：分层抽样要求 y 是离散类别，按类别比例切分；回归的 y 是连续值（房价），没有类别比例可言，所以回归划分只控制 `test_size` 与随机种子。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
